property_summary: A call to sudicideAnyone either reverts or the caller is the test contract itself.
A call to sudicideAnyone either reverts or the caller is the test contract itself.

After a successful call to sudicideAnyone(), the contract C must be destroyed (its code size becomes zero). The reference correctly self-destructs, while the buggy version sends funds to address(0) but fails to self-destruct.

After a successful call to sudicideAnyone() by the owner, the contract's ETH balance must become zero because it selfdestructs and sends all funds to the caller; the buggy version sends to address(0) and leaves the balance unchanged if the contract had no prior ETH.

After the owner calls sudicideAnyone(), the contract's code must be destroyed (code size zero); the buggy version selfdestructs to address(0) but selfdestruct still destroys the contract in the same transaction, so an external view of code size after the call distinguishes them.

After the owner calls sudicideAnyone(), address(this).balance must become 0 because the contract self-destructs and all funds are sent to the caller; the bug sends to address(0) which burns the ether but the contract's balance is still zero, so the difference is that in the reference the owner's balance increases by the contract's prior balance, while in the bug the owner's balance does not increase.

The `__onlyOwner` modifier on `sudicideAnyone` should allow only the owner to self-destruct the contract; the bug always permits it, so any non-owner can destroy the contract, causing owner checks to fail for non-zero non-owner callers.

After any call to sudicideAnyone, the contract should not exist (its code size is zero) if and only if the caller is the owner; the mutant permits non-owners to self-destruct, causing the contract to vanish when it should not.

After any call to sudicideAnyone(), the contract C should still have code (extcodesize > 0) because the caller is always an EOA (non-owner), meaning the require in the reference contract will revert and the selfdestruct will never execute; the mutant, with require(true), allows any caller to successfully selfdestruct, so the contract's code will be destroyed.

For any caller, if the caller is not the owner, then calling sudicideAnyone must NOT result in the contract being destroyed (i.e., the contract code size must remain non-zero). The mutant allows any non-owner to destroy the contract, making the code size zero when it should remain non-zero.
